 Analysis: Familiar problems for toothless Sky Blues 
 Image source, Getty Images By Adam Millington BBC Sport journalist Published 24 October 2026 
 It is early in the season, but Saturday's defeat and Coventry's next match against bottom club Sunderland could likely prove to be a barometer for how strong Frank Lampard's side are. 
 They endured a tough start to life back in the top flight but picked up back-to-back victories before being beaten 3-1 by Tottenham on Monday in a match where the scoreline was arguably harsh.
 Coventry's issues this season clearly lie in front of goal, with four of their six so far having come in their win against Newcastle. They only generated 0.5 expected goals (xG) against Fulham.
 On Saturday, they once again failed to score in the first half - something they have done in seven of their eight league games this term.
 While their counter-attacking style produced some moments of promise, the lack of a clinical edge left them unable to make it count and vulnerable to being punished.
 In particular, they had a sustained period of chances in the second half where they subjected Fulham to continuous waves of attacks but none produced anything of note.
 Defeat leaves them just one place off the bottom of the table.
